scope: Public default-branch source and repository metadata, plus explicitly identified tagged release source; not installed releases or runtime interoperability.

Map-first social app. The public repository contains store metadata and releases, not its private implementation. “Active” describes that public metadata only; no source-backed protocol generation can be assigned.

Family-video prototype. Its native bridge manifest and lockfile pin MIP-era MDK 0.7.1 at 8a8d06c19d617394b0e268f5f9adfad34db3cdf6, and bridge source uses NostrGroupConfigData. The README lists sharing/sync as unfinished; the repository name does not establish Marmot v2. Last commit: 2026-05-24.

Private location sharing for Android and iOS. The core now pins the post-MIP engine/session/storage at MDK fcc85edd8dbd07c8293c899ee52230f72c54c897 (0.10.4); runtime uses AccountDeviceSession. This establishes v2 source adoption, not compatibility with every subsequent v2 profile or installed release.

Dockerized REST service. Lockfile resolves @internet-privacy/marmot-ts 0.4.0; the registry archive matches the lockfile SHA-512 integrity and contains the MIP-01 MarmotGroupData custom extension (0xf2ee), not v2 app components. Last commit: 2026-04-05.
Older integration using the standalone Python MDK binding API; distinct from MDK's current first-party connector. Last commit: 2026-05-27.
Agent bridge whose documented setup still uses the superseded White Noise Rust daemon. Last commit: 2026-06-27.
Container wrapper around the older community CLI. Last commit: 2026-03-02.

Group location sharing and chat. Both iOS and Android current source target the unreleased 2.0.0 Marmot v2 migration and pin MarmotKit 0.11.0 in their vendoring scripts. The latest public GitHub release remains v1.11.2 (Marmot v1). Old groups do not migrate; account identity is retained. Source support does not establish a released v2 build or cross-client interoperability.

Separate community plugin whose documented tkhumush/marmot-cli engine uses the old MDK and NostrGroupConfigData API. Its v1 source expectation is verified; an unpinned upstream branch and configurable executable do not prove a particular installed binary or working current build. Last commit: 2026-05-16.

Nostr Android/desktop client and amy terminal client. Current source pins separately published Quartz 2.13.0, marmot-kmp 2.2.1 and mls-kmp 1.3.0. Marmot and MLS have independent repositories and release lifecycles. Source inspection only.

Active standalone Kotlin Multiplatform Nostr library, including Marmot event types. MLS and Marmot engine behavior lives in separate mls-kmp and marmot-kmp libraries, so this repository is adjacent supporting infrastructure. This replaces the historical empty-repository snapshot.

Android find-my-device fork of FMD with a Marmot command channel. The bridge now pins marmot-app, marmot-account, cgka-engine, cgka-session and storage-sqlite at MDK fcc85ed (Release MDK 0.10.4); the lock resolves 0.10.4. This supersedes the 2026-10-01 record (registry mdk-core 0.8.0 at 4ac6235). Archive status was not returned by the inspected project API. No installation or interoperability test performed.

Native Odin MLS and Marmot engine implementing v2 account identity proofs and application-component profiles. Current README targets byte compatibility with MDK 0.12.0; full mixed-engine interoperability and independent security review remain open release gates. Production readiness is not claimed.

Family Bitcoin wallet. The Marmot integration from PR 1163 was merged into the default branch on 2026-10-09; the README lists Marmot (MLS over Nostr, Alpha) one-to-one and group chats beside NIP-17. package.json vendors a marmot-ts 0.6.1 pre-release tarball whose SHA-512 matches the lockfile; it was read without executing and implements v2 application components and the 0x8009 account identity proof. The session service constructs a MarmotClient. The repository moved from BenGWeeks to the LightningPiggy organization with the same GitHub repository id. Released builds were not inspected; no installation or interoperability test performed.

Groundhog is the GNOME GTK4/libadwaita messenger in the nostrc monorepo, using its C libmarmot implementation. The tagged alpha5 source supports the adopted Marmot v2 profile with app components and account identity proof 0x8009, alongside legacy-profile groups. Its MLS service creates adopted groups when that KeyPackage format is selected. The default-branch profile header matches the inspected release blob. The README documents NIP-17 private messages and local Grotto/NIP-55L or remote NIP-46 signers. Activity is repository-level. Alpha maturity and documented unsupported protocol operations remain; no hands-on test or blanket interoperability claim is made.

Browser/PWA messenger using marmot-ts 0.8.0, with encrypted group media/calls and in-chat games. Current source adds signed nsite publication; localStorage key custody and untested White Noise interoperability remain limitations.

Independent Common Lisp MLS/Marmot library and CLI; components include account identity proof 0x8009 and encrypted-media-v2. README reports wn interop, not independently run. Dependencies natrium, secp256k1-fast, seal, cl-nostr and bordeaux-threads are ASDF/local siblings, not locked; README mentions cl-nostr marmot-rumors branch. No immutable dependency binding.

Authenticated execution agent with optional cl-marmot transport. Concrete attach-marmot invokes CREATE/OPEN-ACCOUNT, PUBLISH-KEY-PACKAGE, ADD-HANDLER, MESSAGE-SENDER, SEND. No version lock for optional cl-marmot: v2 classification is current compatible dependency path, not frozen reproducible installed release. README explicitly new unaudited research software, sandbox is state isolation not capability isolation; principals have shell-equivalent power.

Independent adopted component-based protocol; directory v2 alone is NOT evidence (README says fork marker). Actual 0x8009 proof, app_data_dictionary/app_components and component IDs support v2. Quartz event dependency com.vitorpamplona.quartz:quartz:1.14.0; own MLS stack not inherited Quartz MLS. README says only JVM builds; Android/native targets broken, not Maven published, known convergence/restart/persistence gaps. Reported398 tests not independently executed.

Nostr event-coordination PWA and native Android app with coordinator-managed Marmot event chat. Android fetch tooling pins MarmotKit 0.14.0; the vendored TypeScript runtime is marmot-ts 0.9.0 at 039016cb972a59a9f75029d671892867ae891700. Experimental source; runtime interoperability not independently exercised.
Supabase-style Nostr record SDK; experimental encrypted shared collections via Marmot, with Fieldwork demo. No independent audit or released White Noise interoperability established.

TypeScript Nostr relay whose default branch implements Marmot event handling rather than only generic storage. Kinds: 443 (MIP-00 legacy KeyPackage), 10051 (MIP-00 relay list, replaceable), 30443 (MIP-00 addressable KeyPackage with d-tag deduplication), 444 (MIP-02 Welcome rumor, blocked from direct publishing and required to arrive inside a kind 1059 gift wrap), and 445 (MIP-03 Group Event, validated to carry exactly one 64-character lowercase hex h tag so #h subscriptions resolve). package.json declares supportedMips [0, 1, 2, 3], emitted as supported_mips in the NIP-11 relay information document. It is a relay, not a messaging implementation: it performs no MLS, which is why it is labelled adjacent rather than v1 or v2. No hands-on relay test or group interoperability claim is made.

Linux/macOS HERDR bridge for existing OpenCode, Codex and Claude Code sessions. connector.toml pins MDK 0.14.0 revision 3fb4b4759ac676b0c21c4c3527074866c9fa4c89 with a local patch. Supports images, local voice transcription, direct mid-turn text delivery and editable progress through wn-agent. Source inspected; runtime interoperability was not tested.

CLI/TUI and Tauri desktop messenger. Pins a post-MIP MDK v0.9.20 fork with SOCKS5 support for relays and media. Maintainer declares maintenance mode. Desktop packages unsigned; runtime interoperability not tested in this audit.

Experimental Fedimint wallet PWA with actual MDK-backed Marmot chat via a browser Worker/WASI runtime. Pins post-MIP cgka-engine and transport-nostr-peeler. Maintainer warns against production use or real funds; wallet recovery remains unproven. No runtime interoperability test performed in this audit.

Browser/PWA and Android Bitcoin wallet with Ark, Lightning and on-chain balances, and a Nostr client. Its own JavaScript MLS/Marmot layer implements the v2 application-component dictionary and account identity proof 0x8009. Features and protocol are source-verified; no wallet safety or cross-client interoperability claim is made.

Static-site Nostr messenger with no backend. Forward-secret groups of up to 100 use its own Marmot-format layer on ts-mls 1.6.4: kinds 30443/444/445, the 0x0006 application-data dictionary and profile/admin components, citing the specification's foundation and app-components documents. DMs and small groups use NIP-17. The README states the code is not independently audited. No interoperability test performed.

Wizard OS alpha app with a Marmot text-chat engine on MDK 0.12 and a unified Matrix/Telegram inbox, HTTP API, MCP and editable web view. The unified history is stored in plaintext on the local machine; Telegram cloud chats do not inherit Marmot end-to-end encryption. Current README documents Wizard AppStore alpha installation. Runtime behavior was not tested.

Operator-free messaging, Lightning/Solana payments and NIP-90 AI jobs in a single-file web app with Tauri launchers (German README). Its packages/mls module compiles MDK to WebAssembly from upstream revision a19feca with a local patch; the lock resolves cgka-engine and marmot-app 0.10.4. The app's MLS engine loads that module for group and one-to-one forward-secret encryption. How much of the app's chat uses it was not traced; no runtime test performed.

Tor-only Marmot client and authenticated Nostr relay for anonymous one-to-one dead drops, served as one v3 onion service. Engine crates (cgka-engine, cgka-traits, transport-nostr-peeler) come from the Epiphytic/mdk fork at 4981e59, an upstream MDK commit with workspace version 0.9.15. The repository is organised around feasibility gates with dated results; maturity is prototype. No Tor or interoperability test performed.

Sends private Frigate person alerts (a snapshot, then buffered video) to a White Noise group through a dedicated bot using MDK's wn/wnd CLI; build-mdk.sh pins MDK 1016a76 from 2026-10-13. README status: initial implementation validated with synthetic events and media; a real Frigate installation, relay publication and phone delivery await the owner's verification. A community integration in the Marmot organization, not an official Frigate or MDK component.

Remote-command project being rebuilt in native Rust on upstream MDK and embedded Arti. Current v0.2 source and direct command/restart probes are distinct from the legacy Python v0.1 prereleases. Installed cross-platform command acceptance and public v0.2 publication remain pending; Arti command attempts are deferred to v0.3. No installation or interoperability test performed for this catalog.

Coding-agent control plane in early development. Current commands cover platform/setup/configuration and the admind recovery service, which connects a privileged admin agent through MDK wn-agent. The planned wsd/workstream adapters remain absent. Source inspection only.

Marmot group-history debugger from the marmot-ts maintainer: a headless member that, once invited, sets retention and fork horizons to infinity, keeps every fork of a group and renders its history as a branching timeline in a small web UI. Built on the marmot-ts submodule at a48a0ef (package 0.6.0, v2 components and identity proof). The author's signed NIP-34 announcement lists this GitHub repository as a clone URL. Adjacent because it is diagnostic tooling, not a messenger.

Guided Nostr diagnostic and repair tool. Its Marmot coverage, reviewed against specification commit 4a2bc65 on 2026-09-06, validates public kind-30443 KeyPackages, including MLS capabilities, the 0x0006 dictionary and component 0x8009 identity proofs. A separate Legacy Marmot Cleanup section handles kind 443 and 10051 events. Diagnostics only; it does not implement messaging.

Relay-on-demand service where each name under bind.ws is a claimable Nostr relay. An opt-in Marmot transport accepts kind-30443 KeyPackages and opaque kind-445 group messages after checking only their tags and encoding. A KeyPackage must advertise the 0x8009 identity-proof component, but the proof inside the opaque MLS content is not verified by the relay. Account admission and storage caps apply to ephemeral authors; clients manage encryption, proof verification and membership. Relay support only, not a messaging implementation; runtime behaviour untested.
Standalone Kotlin Multiplatform Marmot library extracted from Amethyst; its README documents the current Marmot profile and the independent mls-kmp engine.
Standalone Kotlin Multiplatform RFC 9420 engine used by marmot-kmp. Nostr-independent MLS dependency, not a Marmot implementation.

Kotlin Multiplatform collaboration app for translation workgroups and threshold-signing approvals. The app imports MIP-01 MarmotGroupData and pins Quartz 1.14.0. Its Maven Central source archive implements the 0xf2ee NostrGroupData extension and BasicCredential identity matching, establishing the older MIP profile rather than post-MIP application components. Its in-group private messages require a documented MIP-03 author-check carve-out in other clients; stock clients may reject them. Runtime interoperability and released builds were not tested.

Unofficial Python standard-library CLI for sending notifications and files through an existing local wn-agent. Its Unix-socket requests and responses use marmot.agent-control.v2. The v2 label follows this current MDK transport boundary; it is not an independent MLS implementation. Runtime delivery was not tested.

Browser relay evaluator with NIP-11 checks and kind-30443 publication/query probes. The probe creates an empty synthetic KeyPackage-shaped event: relay acceptance does not establish cryptographically valid MLS KeyPackage support. No relay mutation or interoperability test performed. Last commit: 2026-07-11.

Android Labradorite and Linux agentd now use the independent marmot-kmp 2.2.1 engine and Quartz 2.7.3, replacing the former Rust MDK runtime. Custom inner events 7770/7771 carry agent controls; kind-9 prompts and final answers keep conversations readable in White Noise. Native coding runtimes and phone controls remain separate from messaging generation. Source inspected; interoperability not tested.

MarmotKit 0.14.0 client with its own identity, group invitations, encrypted audio/text sends and received-message handling. Early release v0.1.1 has an APK. Android 12 or newer; Marmot messaging requires ARM64. Transcription uses a separate OSTT app. Source inspected; runtime interoperability and security were not tested.

Bitcoin wallet with a MarmotKit-backed group-wallet transport on Android and desktop. Native bridge and Android build helper pin MDK 20ded88b166b685a23754a168f7d1514fb96b9ce (0.15.0-dev); the Tauri app registers the plugin and its group reducer uses invitations and encrypted wallet messages. Early mainnet alpha, unaudited; messaging can be unavailable when native bridge assets are absent. No installation, wallet safety or interoperability test performed.

Experimental secure-application SDK with isolated Marmot/OpenMLS interoperability probes. Its exact-pin Phase B verdict documents synthetic direct-MLS tests with an MDK peer, not general Marmot conformance or production product activation. Classified as supporting interoperability research, not as a v2 messenger. Results are publisher-reported and were not rerun.
